entities.summary: Artemisia Lomi Gentileschi was an Italian Baroque painter. Gentileschi is considered among the most accomplished 17th-century artists, initially working in the style of Caravaggio. She was producing professional work by the age of 15. In an era when women had few opportunities to pursue artistic training or work as professional artists, Gentileschi was the first woman to become a member of the Accademia di Arte del Disegno in Florence and she had an international clientele. Gentileschi worked as an expatriate painter in the court of Charles I of England from 1638 to 1642, but she is thought to have fled the country in the early phases of the English Civil War.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As one of the first women to achieve professional success as an artist in a male-dominated field, Artemisia Gentileschi paved the way for future generations of female artists. Her work had significant regional impact, influencing the development of Baroque art and challenging societal norms around gender and artistic ability.
